themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints skyrocketed to 97 THIS WEEK—a 308% spike versus the 23.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.85)—suggesting a sudden, district-wide pavement or infrastructure failure affecting Upper East Side mobility and safety.
evidence: 97 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 23.8 weekly average (308% spike, z-score: 5.85)
This represents the single largest percentage increase across all tracked complaint categories this week
Aligns with CB budget history of repeated requests to 'Repair or build new step streets' (DOT), suggesting chronic underlying infrastructure issues now acute
reporting_angles: Map the 97 complaints geographically to identify hotspot blocks; interview DOT on cause (freeze-thaw damage, deferred maintenance, construction)
Canvass affected blocks with photos of potholes, broken curbs, or displaced pavement; interview elderly residents and delivery workers on safety hazards

themes_detail.label: Building Maintenance Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints jumped to 22 LAST WEEK—a 403% spike from the 4.4-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 4.67)—indicating a sudden wave of NYCHA or private building upkeep failures across the district.
evidence: 22 maintenance/facility complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average (403% spike, z-score: 4.67)
Flooring/Stairs complaints also elevated at 12 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 4.8 baseline (153% spike, z-score: 4.9)
CB budget requests show 6+ annual requests for 'Renovate or upgrade public housing developments' and 'NYCHA community facilities,' signaling systemic deferred maintenance
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint details to identify which buildings/developments are generating the spike; interview NYCHA residents on specific failures (leaks, broken elevators, broken stairs)
Cross-reference with DOB alteration permits (1523 filed in 90 days) to determine if complaints are from delayed or incomplete work

themes_detail.label: Street Light Infrastructure Failure
themes_detail.summary: Street Light Condition complaints spiked to 19 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 176% jump from the 6.9-complaint weekly average (z-score: 5.5)—raising public safety concerns around nighttime visibility and crime deterrence on Upper East Side blocks.
evidence: 19 street light complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 6.9 weekly average (176% spike, z-score: 5.5)
Street light failures compound with the concurrent street condition spike (308% this week), creating compounded mobility and safety hazards
Recent subway safety incident (Gothamist, 2026-03-26) underscores resident concern about public safety infrastructure
reporting_angles: Request ConEd/NYCDOT data on outages and repair timelines for the affected two-week period; identify which blocks are dark
Interview NYPD precinct on whether officers report correlation between outages and street crime reports; speak to residents about perceived safety

themes_detail.label: Taxi Complaint Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Taxi complaints jumped to 25 LAST WEEK—a 133% spike from the 10.8-complaint weekly average (z-score: 5.06)—suggesting emerging issues with illegal parking, reckless driving, or taxi stand violations affecting commuters and pedestrians.
evidence: 25 taxi complaints LAST WEEK vs. 10.8 weekly average (133% spike, z-score: 5.06)
Illegal Parking remains the 2nd largest complaint category overall (1536 in 90 days), and taxi-related complaints may be a subset of that trend
Real-time Enforcement complaints also spiked to 6 THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 baseline (243% spike), possibly indicating enforcement response to taxi violations
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint text summaries to determine whether spike is driven by illegal taxi stands, double-parking, or reckless behavior; map hot spots
Interview TLC enforcement, local precinct, and residents on Madison/Park Avenues (common taxi corridors) about what sparked the increase

themes_detail.label: Asbestos & Building Material Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints peaked at 5 THREE WEEKS AGO—a 700% spike from the 0.6-complaint baseline (z-score: 5.11)—suggesting discovery of hazardous materials in renovations or demolitions, with 1698 building alteration permits filed in the district in the past 90 days.
evidence: 5 asbestos complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.11)
1698 building alteration permits filed in 90 days (1523 alterations, 22 demolitions) provide many opportunities for asbestos discovery during construction
Flooring/stairs complaints (153% spike) may indicate unsafe conditions in buildings undergoing renovation where asbestos was disturbed
reporting_angles: Request DOB database to identify which buildings filed the asbestos complaints and cross-reference with active alteration/demolition permits; interview residents on exposure

Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection and NYC Health on protocols for asbestos discovery during construction; speak to contractors/safety experts on whether spike reflects real increase in exposures or better reporting
